title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-02-05
lineage: SBD MR > C > D > CD + AUD low-gen

ai_review.summary: Matrix source with good‑ish soundboard clarity captures a smoking Feb 5 1970 show – Mason’s Children and the Eleven→Caution sequence are highlights.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised as one of the band’s peak early‑70 shows, with Mason’s Children, The Eleven, Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) and the China Cat > I Know You Rider segue getting special love.  Recording quality is mixed – the first few tracks are audience‑sourced and a few soundboard sections are muddy or bass‑light, but overall the matrix mix is listenable and lets the strong drumming and keyboard work shine through.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and rave about the musical performance; recording issues are noted but not enough to outweigh the strong show, yielding a high overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: First four tracks are audience recordings (acceptable for their age).  The bulk is soundboard but some sections are muddy with dead spots and the bass a bit low; treble can be harsh, occasional drop‑outs.  Overall clarity is sufficient to enjoy the performance.

standout_songs: The Eleven > Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider (missing from the tape)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set opens with acoustic numbers, builds into a powerful Mason's Children and The Eleven jam, then rolls smoothly through Caution into a tight Not Fade Away → Cumberland Blues close, praised for its seamless transitions and high‑energy mid‑set.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead guitar is highlighted throughout; a brief Speedway Boogie‑style jam appears inside Big Boss Man and he even dabbles on pedal steel in two George Jones cuts.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh delivers an “amazing” bass line during the second Mason's Children instrumental; his aggressive riffing drives Caution and he takes charge during its chaotic ending.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s rhythm work shines especially in the Mason's Children jam, complementing Lesh’s improvisation.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen is noted on organ for The Eleven (a rare and emotional moment) and adds claves on Uncle John's Band; keyboards are generally clear and vibrant.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum mix receives repeated praise – described as “fantastic,” “popping, crunching, jitter‑y,” with a bright, punchy sound that lifts the whole performance.
